topic: The DNA of Space: From Linear Combinations to Bases
target_audience: University students beginning Linear Algebra or advanced high school students

sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Instructions
lecture_lines: Think of vectors as instructions for movement.
Vector v moves us east and north.
Scaling v stretches or shrinks this movement.
animations: Create a 2D grid and a vector v (#00FFFF) from (0,0) to (1,2). Label it 'Movement'.
Move a small dot [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/dot.svg] along v. Highlight horizontal component (+1) and vertical component (+2) with dashed lines.
Show vector v stretching to 2v and shrinking to 0.5v along its original line.

sections.title: The Recipe: Linear Combinations
lecture_lines: Combine instructions by scaling and adding them.
Scale vector v and w independently.
Their sum is called a linear combination.
Weights determine the contribution of each vector.
This arithmetic builds every path in space.
animations: Show vectors v (#00FFFF) and w (#FFFF00) starting at the origin.
Animate v scaling to 1.5v and w scaling to 2w. Label them with their weights.
Shift the scaled vector 2w to the tip of 1.5v. Draw the resultant vector sum z (#FFFFFF).
Display the formula z = c1v + c2w. Highlight scalars c1 and c2 in #FFA500 as they pulse.
Animate the resultant vector z moving to various points as c1 and c2 vary, leaving a trail.

sections.title: The Reach: What is a Span?
lecture_lines: What if we use every possible scaling factor?
All resulting points form the vector's span.
Two non-parallel vectors can span a plane.
Span represents the reach of your set.
Varying coefficients paints the entire reachable space.
animations: Vectors v (#00FFFF) and w (#FFFF00) appear. Scale them by random factors.
A grid of points (#888888) starts appearing at the tips of various linear combinations.

A paintbrush [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/paintbrush.svg] moves across the screen as the points merge into a continuous light-blue shaded region (#ADD8E6) covering the 2D plane.
Display the text label 'Span' in the center of the shaded region.
The shaded region expands outwards to fill the entire screen, representing infinite reach.

sections.title: The Redundancy: Linear Dependence
lecture_lines: Some vectors don't add new directions.
If one vector is redundant, they're dependent.
Independent vectors each provide a unique path.
animations: Show two vectors v (#00FFFF) and w (#FFFF00) spanning a 2D plane.
Introduce a third vector u (#FF00FF) that lies exactly on the plane (e.g., u = v + w).
Label u as 'Redundant' and show it provides no new directions to the span.

sections.title: The Goldilocks Set: Defining a Basis
lecture_lines: A basis is a perfect, efficient toolkit.
It must span the entire target space.
It must also be linearly independent.
No redundant vectors, yet every point reachable.
This minimal set defines the coordinate system.
animations: Show a set of two vectors b1 (#00FFFF) and b2 (#FFFF00). Label the set 'Basis' and incorporate the toolkit icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/toolkit.svg] to represent the fundamental building blocks.
Animate b1 and b2 sweeping out the entire 2D plane to demonstrate span.
Flash the vectors in #FFFFFF to emphasize they are not parallel (linearly independent).
Show a target point P and show the unique combination of b1 and b2 that reaches it.
Transition the basis vectors into a standard coordinate grid.

sections.title: Summary and Geometric Wrap-up
lecture_lines: Combinations are tools; Span is the territory.
Independence ensures no wasted movement instructions.
Together, they form the space's unique DNA.
animations: Show a split screen: one side displaying vector addition, the other showing a shaded plane (Span).
Show three vectors in 2D; one disappears, but the shaded span area remains unchanged.
The remaining two basis vectors expand into a full grid with the text 'The DNA of Space' and the dna icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/dna.svg].
